independence: Each role was filled by separate fresh claude-opus-5-5 sessions (subject x3, safety x2, language x2, lessons split by count), each given only its own role's work orders (openlessons jury orders) and told never to open another role's orders or verdicts; verdicts were written to per-role folders and combined only by jury run after all seven sessions had finished. The drafting model (claude-fable-5) sat on no role.

notes: subject: 'When do we sleep?' is a habit question, not science about why day and night happen, and the distractor 'दोपहर में' is also defensible (many children nap in the afternoon). Replace with an item on the objective, e.g. which side of the Earth has night.

claims.claim: About half of the Earth faces the Sun and has daytime; the lit part changes as the Earth rotates on its axis, which causes day and night.

notes: safety: 'When do we sleep?' marks 'in the afternoon' wrong, but afternoon naps are normal for 5-6-year-olds (and common in Indian homes), and some children live with night-shift carers who sleep by day; it tells a child their own routine is wrong. Reword (e.g. 'When is it dark outside?') or ask about most people at night.
